description: Forty students are chosen from across Canada each year to work on the floor of the House of Commons while doing their first year of university in Ottawa. Pages carry documents and messages during sittings, work directly around Members of Parliament and see federal legislation as it happens, which is experience almost nothing else at that age can match. Recruitment runs on a long cycle: applications for the 2027 to 2028 cohort open in September 2026 and close in November 2026, selections finish in March 2027 and offers go out at the end of April 2027. You apply in your Grade 12 year, so the timing lines up with university applications.

name: City of Edmonton Youth Council
grades: High school and post-secondary age youth in Edmonton
duration: Appointed term of roughly one to two years, with monthly meetings plus committee work
location: Edmonton (meetings at City Hall, first Wednesday of the month, 5:30 to 8:30 pm)
eligibility: Edmonton youth appointed by City Council through an annual recruitment normally held in May. The age range and residency terms are set in each year's posting, so email youthcouncil@edmonton.ca for the current criteria.
description: The City of Edmonton Youth Council ended on August 31, 2026. City Council dissolved it that spring along with six other advisory boards, after nearly three decades of youth members writing policy proposals and advising Council on issues affecting young Edmontonians. Other Alberta municipalities still run youth councils or advisory committees, so check your own city or town's civic agency listings for one that is recruiting.
metaDescription: Ended August 31, 2026, when Edmonton City Council dissolved it with six other advisory boards. Look for a youth council in your own town.

name: Vimy Pilgrimage Award
duration: About one week in April, plus preparation before departure
stipend: Fully funded, including travel, accommodation and all program costs
eligibility: Canadian youth aged 15 to 17 with a demonstrated record of service to their community. Competitive written application; no cost to recipients.
description: A fully funded week in Belgium and France studying Canada's role in the First World War on the ground, visiting battlefields, cemeteries and museums with a national cohort of students. It rewards community service and historical interest rather than marks, and it carries real weight on a scholarship application later. The 2026 journey ran April 3 to 11 and its application window was October 21 to November 25, 2025. The next cycle had not been posted as of August 2026, so watch the page from mid-October.
metaDescription: A fully funded week in Belgium and France studying Canada's role in the First World War, visiting battlefields, cemeteries and museums.
costNote: No cost to recipients

name: Calgary Youth Science Fair (CYSF)
provider: Calgary Youth Science Fair Society / Youth Science Canada
location: Calgary (in-person, University of Calgary Olympic Oval)
eligibility: Calgary-area students in grades 5-12, entered through a school coordinator or as an independent entrant
description: Canada's largest regional science fair. Schools register October 1 to December 4 and independent entrants from December 10; every project must be registered with its ethics forms by February 4. Winning here is the route to the Canada-Wide Science Fair for Calgary students.
metaDescription: Canada's largest regional science fair, at the Olympic Oval April 8-10, 2027. Projects and ethics forms must be registered by February 4.

name: Edmonton Regional Science Fair (ERSF)
provider: Edmonton Regional Science Fair Council / Youth Science Canada
duration: Year-long project + two-day fair in March
eligibility: Students whose home or school address falls in the Edmonton region
description: The qualifying fair for Edmonton students heading to the Canada-Wide Science Fair. The 2026 edition ran March 14 to 15 with registration open January 9 to February 28; the council had not posted 2027 dates when this was checked, so expect the same late-winter shape.
metaDescription: Edmonton's qualifying route to the Canada-Wide Science Fair. The 2026 fair ran in March with a late-February deadline; 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Central Alberta Regional Science Fair (CARSF)
provider: Central Alberta Regional Science Fair / Youth Science Canada
eligibility: Central Alberta students; experimental, innovation or research projects accepted
description: One fair day at Red Deer Polytechnic on March 20, 2027, with setup the evening before. A $10 entry fee applies per project, payable on or after the fair, and up to six of the top senior projects advance to the Canada-Wide Science Fair. Registration had not reopened when this was checked.
metaDescription: One day at Red Deer Polytechnic on March 20, 2027. A $10 entry fee applies, and up to six senior projects advance to the Canada-Wide Science Fair.
costNote: $10 entry fee per project

name: Sci-Fusion: Lethbridge Regional Science Fair and Science Olympics
grades: Grades K-12 (grades 7-12 advance to the national fair)
duration: Year-long project + two-day event in spring
eligibility: Students in grades K-12 at southwestern Alberta schools
description: Two events in one weekend: the Lethbridge Regional Science Fair and the Science Olympics, a same-day design and build competition. Top projects in grades 7 to 12 are invited to the Canada-Wide Science Fair. The 2026 edition ran April 10 to 11; SATC had not posted 2027 dates when this was checked.
metaDescription: The Lethbridge regional fair and Science Olympics in one weekend, open to southwestern Alberta students in grades K-12. The 2027 date is not posted.

name: Wood Buffalo Regional Science Fair (WBRSF)
provider: Wood Buffalo Regional Science Fair / Youth Science Canada
duration: Year-long project + two-day fair in late March
eligibility: Students throughout the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo
description: Fort McMurray's qualifying fair, judged on a Friday with public viewing and awards the Saturday after. Sponsors cover the cost so entry is free to students, and finalists from the junior, intermediate and senior pools advance to the Canada-Wide Science Fair. The 2026 judging ran March 27.
metaDescription: Fort McMurray's route to the Canada-Wide Science Fair, open to grades 4-12 across the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo. Sponsors keep entry free.
costNote: Sponsors cover the cost; entry is free to students

name: Peace Country Regional Science Fair (PCRSF)
provider: Peace Country Regional Science Fair / Youth Science Canada
duration: Year-long project + one fair day in late March
eligibility: Students at northwest Alberta schools, judged in grade 5/6, 7/8, 9/10 and 11/12 divisions
description: The qualifying fair for northwest Alberta, and the route to the Canada-Wide Science Fair for students around Peace River, Slave Lake and Valleyview. The 42nd fair ran March 25, 2026 with registration closing March 10, and five finalists went on to nationals in Edmonton. Organisers have said they expect a 2027 fair but had not posted its dates when this was checked.
metaDescription: Northwest Alberta's route to the Canada-Wide Science Fair, judged in divisions from grade 5 to 12. The 2026 fair sent five finalists to nationals.

name: Alberta Innovates Summer Research Studentships – University of Calgary
duration: 8, 12 or 16 weeks between May and August
eligibility: Graduating Grade 12 students with at least an 85% average and a clear interest in a health research career; you must first secure a full-time UCalgary faculty supervisor
description: A paid summer in a UCalgary health research lab the summer after Grade 12, funded by Alberta Innovates. You find a faculty supervisor first, then apply together. Applications open November 23, 2026 and close January 25, 2027; students without a UCalgary ID request one first.
metaDescription: Paid health research at UCalgary the summer after Grade 12, up to $7,500. Find a faculty supervisor first.

name: Alberta Envirothon
stipend: Cash prizes and trophies for the top three teams
eligibility: Teams of five high school students with one or two advisers, from schools or clubs across Alberta
description: A three-day environmental science competition. Teams of five work through field stations and written tests in aquatic ecology, forestry, soils and land use, wildlife and a current issue, then give an oral presentation. The winning team represents Alberta at the international NCF-Envirothon.
metaDescription: Teams of five compete in ecology, forestry, soils and wildlife over three days in May. The winner represents Alberta internationally.

name: Canadian Senior and Intermediate Mathematics Contests
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
location: School-based across Alberta (written at your own school)
eligibility: Grades 9–10 write the Intermediate and grades 11–12 the Senior; a contest supervisor at the school orders and supervises
description: The CEMC's November contests, with full-solution questions alongside short answers. A step up from Pascal, Cayley and Fermat and a common route toward the Canadian Open Mathematics Challenge. Schools order by October 22, 2026 for the November 18, 2026 contest.
metaDescription: Two-hour CEMC contests in November: Intermediate for grades 9–10, Senior for 11–12, written at your school.
costNote: $14 per participant plus school order and shipping fees

name: Beaver Computing Challenge
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
location: School-based across Alberta (written at your own school)
eligibility: Students in Grade 10 or below; no programming experience needed. A contest supervisor at the school registers participants
description: A computational-thinking contest with no coding: logic and problem-solving puzzles built on the math students already know. A gentle first step before the Canadian Computing Competition. Schools register by October 26, 2026 for the November 9–20, 2026 window.
metaDescription: A 45-minute computational-thinking contest for Grade 10 and below, built on logic puzzles with no coding needed.
costNote: $3 per participant plus a $5 processing fee per order

name: Fryer, Galois and Hypatia Mathematics Contests
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
location: School-based across Alberta (written at your own school)
eligibility: Students in grades 9, 10 and 11 respectively; a contest supervisor at the school orders and supervises
description: Four-question contests where the written solution counts, not just the answer: good practice for proof-style problems. Schools order by March 11, 2027 for the April 7, 2027 contests.
metaDescription: CEMC's full-solution contests for grades 9, 10 and 11: four questions in 75 minutes, written at your school in April.
costNote: $12 per participant plus $5 processing and $5 shipping per order

name: Canadian Team Mathematics Contest
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
duration: One day in April (individual, team and relay rounds)
location: At your own school, or at the University of Waterloo by lottery
eligibility: Teams of six secondary students in any mix of grades 9–12, with an educator supervisor
description: A team math contest for six students, run as an in-school event on or after April 14, 2027, or at the University of Waterloo by lottery. Schools order the in-school version by April 12, 2027; the Waterloo lottery closes November 19, 2026.
metaDescription: Six-student math teams in any mix of grades 9–12 compete each April, at your school or at the University of Waterloo.
costNote: $50 per school for the in-school event (unlimited teams), plus a $5 processing fee

name: North American Computational Linguistics Open (NACLO)
provider: NACLO, hosted in Alberta by the University of Alberta's Alberta Language Technology Lab
duration: 3-hour Open Round in late January; invitational round in March
location: Host sites, including the University of Alberta North Campus in Edmonton
eligibility: High school students in the US and Canada; register at naclo.org
description: Linguistics puzzles: work out how an unfamiliar language works from a handful of examples, no prior linguistics needed. The 2027 Open Round is January 28, 2027. The top four Anglophone Canadian students in the invitational round represent Canada at the International Linguistics Olympiad.
metaDescription: Solve puzzles about unfamiliar languages, no background needed. Open Round January 28, 2027, with a site at the U of A.

name: National Biology Competition – University of Toronto
provider: University of Toronto (Ecology & Evolutionary Biology, Cell & Systems Biology)
eligibility: Any secondary school student; the school creates an account and buys seats (minimum 5 students), then students register with a key
description: A national biology exam written online each April, covering biochemistry, cells, metabolism and genetics at a senior high school level. Schools with five or more students are also ranked as teams.
metaDescription: A 75-minute national biology exam written online each April. Your school buys seats, minimum five students.
costNote: $7 CAD per student, minimum 5 students per school

name: Rotary Youth Leadership Awards (RYLA) – Central and Southern Alberta
location: Central and Southern Alberta (and western Saskatchewan)
eligibility: High school students aged 15–17 from Central and Southern Alberta and western Saskatchewan. Most are sponsored by a local Rotary club; independent delegates can also register
description: A weekend leadership conference for 70 to 100 high school students, held every May, with workshops and networking with other young leaders. There is no cost to attend: a local Rotary club sponsors each delegate. Contact a Rotary club near you, or register as an independent delegate.
metaDescription: A free May leadership weekend for 70 to 100 Alberta students aged 15–17. A local Rotary club sponsors you.

name: Rotary Youth Leadership Experience (RYLE) – Northern Alberta
eligibility: High school students from Rotary District 5370, which covers Northern Alberta and parts of Saskatchewan, BC and the NWT
description: A four-day leadership camp at Camp Nakamun with workshops and speakers on interpersonal growth, communication and community building, on a challenge-by-choice basis. The 2026 camp ran April 30 to May 3. Local Rotary clubs sponsor students; ask a club near you about covering the fee.
metaDescription: A four-day spring leadership camp at Camp Nakamun for northern Alberta students in grades 9–12, sponsored by Rotary clubs.
costNote: $500 per student; Rotary clubs sponsor students

name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
grades: High school (open to students in any country)
duration: Several online contests from January to March, 4–5 hours each
eligibility: Anyone can compete with a free account at usaco.org. Only US students are eligible for the training camp and US team
description: A free online programming contest with four divisions, Bronze to Platinum: you start in Bronze and a strong score promotes you. Canadians can compete in every division, making it good practice alongside the Canadian Computing Competition. The 2025–26 season ran three contests from January to February plus a proctored US Open in March; 2026–27 dates are not yet posted.
metaDescription: A free online programming contest, Bronze to Platinum, open to students anywhere. Good practice beside the CCC.

name: Canada/USA Mathcamp
location: A US college campus (2026: Champlain College, Burlington, Vermont)
eligibility: Mathematically talented students aged 13–18 from any country. Admission is by the Qualifying Quiz, a personal essay and a reference; no application fee
description: A residential summer program in university-level mathematics, where students choose their own classes and work on problems with mathematicians. It is free for Canadian families with household incomes under $100,000 USD, with need-based aid above that; aid never affects admission. Dates and location for 2027 are announced in December.
metaDescription: Five weeks of university-level math for ages 13–18. Free for Canadian families under $100,000 USD income.
costNote: $7,500 USD, reduced by need-based aid to as little as $0; free for Canadian households under $100,000 USD

name: TELUS World of Science Volunteering – Edmonton
duration: One 3–4 hour shift a week for three months (about 40 hours)
eligibility: Age 15 or older with Grade 9 Science completed; a police information check with vulnerable sector search is required
description: Volunteer at Edmonton's science centre: welcome visitors, lead hands-on activities and experiments, and explain the space, nature and health galleries. Applications are taken anytime, with intakes in late August, late November and late March.
metaDescription: Lead hands-on science activities at Edmonton's science centre from age 15. Intakes in August, November and March.

name: Avogadro Chemistry Exam
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Advanced Science Education
eligibility: Grade 11 chemistry students at accredited high schools; a teacher registers students
description: The University of Waterloo's Grade 11 chemistry contest, written online at school with a teacher supervising. Teachers register students by April 30, 2027 for the May 13, 2027 exam.
metaDescription: Waterloo's Grade 11 chemistry contest: 40 questions in 75 minutes, written online at your school in May.
costNote: $8 per student

name: Chem 13 News Chemistry Exam
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Advanced Science Education
eligibility: Grade 12 chemistry students at accredited high schools; a teacher registers students
description: The University of Waterloo's senior chemistry contest, the Grade 12 counterpart to the Avogadro exam. Written online at school; teachers register students by April 23, 2027 for the May 6, 2027 exam.
metaDescription: Waterloo's Grade 12 chemistry contest: 40 questions in 75 minutes, written online at your school in May.
costNote: $8 per student

name: Willow River Biology Contest
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Advanced Science Education
eligibility: Grade 11 and 12 biology students at accredited high schools anywhere; a teacher registers students from mid-February
description: A University of Waterloo biology contest on Grade 11 and 12 content, open to schools worldwide. Teachers register students from mid-February until April 9, 2027, for the April 22, 2027 contest.
metaDescription: Waterloo's biology contest on Grade 11 and 12 content: 75 minutes, multiple choice, written at school.
costNote: $4 per student

name: Legislative Assembly of Alberta Page Program
duration: The school year: sittings run February to June and October to December
stipend: $17 an hour
eligibility: Full-time students aged 15 by September 1 and entering Grade 10, 11 or 12, with strong enough marks to miss some class time. At least three shifts a week while the Legislature sits, Monday to Thursday
description: A paid part-time job on the floor of the Alberta Legislature: pages deliver documents to MLAs during sittings, help at public events, and take part in professional development and a speech competition. Recruitment runs each spring; apply with a cover letter, résumé, latest report card, and letters of support from a parent and your school.
metaDescription: A paid job at the Alberta Legislature for students in grades 10–12: $17 an hour, recruited each spring.

name: Mayor's Youth Council – Calgary
provider: Youth Central + The City of Calgary
duration: October to June, about 6 hours a month
eligibility: Calgary junior and senior high students aged 12–18; applications open every fall
description: Calgary's youth council, running since 1992: members meet weekly in subcommittees on civic engagement, careers, health and current issues, hear from guest speakers, meet city officials and plan youth-led events. The 2025–26 council drew from 16 schools across 11 wards. Applications open each fall.
metaDescription: Calgary's youth council for ages 12–18: weekly subcommittees, meetings with city officials, applications each fall.

name: Youth Volunteer Corps – Calgary
duration: Flexible: one-day projects to ongoing ones
eligibility: Calgary youth aged 12–18; no application or interview, just a MyImpact profile and a parent or guardian waiver
description: Hundreds of guided group volunteer projects across Calgary that you sign up for one at a time, with no minimum commitment. After 20 volunteer hours, Youth Central writes you a reference letter, useful for scholarship applications.
metaDescription: Sign up for guided group volunteer projects across Calgary, ages 12–18, and get a reference letter after 20 hours.

name: PROMYS – Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists
eligibility: Ages 14–18, finished Grade 9 and not yet in college full-time. Apply with solutions to the application problem set, a recommendation, a transcript and short answers; international students are welcome
description: Six weeks of deep work in number theory with about 80 high school students and 25 undergraduate counsellors, built around proving results yourself. Applications for 2027 close at the end of February 2027. Aid for Canadian students is case by case, and every applicant can compete for the full-scholarship Breakout Fellowship.
metaDescription: Six residential weeks of number theory at Boston University for ages 14–18. 2027 applications close end of February.
costNote: Up to $8,000 USD (2026); aid for international students is case by case, plus the full-scholarship Breakout Fellowship

name: Ross Mathematics Program
location: Ohio State University (Columbus) or Indiana University (residential)
eligibility: Mostly ages 15–18, occasionally exceptional 14-year-olds; students from outside the US are accepted every year. Apply with essays, a video, a teacher recommendation, a transcript and the application problems
description: A six-week residential summer of number theory built on proving everything yourself, at Ohio State or Indiana University. About 60 first-year students per site are admitted, roughly 15% of applicants. The 2026 deadline was March 8; the program aims to fund every admitted student who needs aid, though aid for international students is limited.
metaDescription: Six weeks of proof-based number theory at Ohio State or Indiana; Canadian students are admitted every year.
costNote: $7,500 USD program fee; need-based aid, limited for international students

name: Child and Youth Advisory Council (CAYAC) – Alberta Children's Hospital
provider: Alberta Health Services – Alberta Children's Hospital
location: Calgary (Alberta Children's Hospital); mileage covered for members from outside Calgary
eligibility: Ages 12–16 with an interest in youth health care, plus at least one of: experience as a patient or a patient's family member, living with a disability or chronic condition, a diverse background, adversity affecting your health, or living in southern Alberta outside greater Calgary
description: Youth volunteers who give Alberta Children's Hospital a youth voice on its programs and services, through consultations and meetings with staff. Recruitment runs each year from June 1 to September 7; apply through the hospital's volunteer portal.
metaDescription: Help shape care at Alberta Children's Hospital from age 12: six Saturday meetings a year, recruited June to September.

name: Stollery Children's Hospital Youth Advisory Council
duration: Six Saturdays each fall (Sep–Nov) and spring (Feb–May)
eligibility: Patients and siblings aged 12–17 who have received care at the Stollery
description: Former patients and their siblings advise the Stollery and Alberta youth health care on programs, policies and platforms. Interviews run through the summer for a September start; apply through the hospital's MyImpact page.
metaDescription: Stollery patients and siblings aged 12–17 advise on youth health care. Interviews each summer for a September start.

name: High School Model United Nations – University of Alberta (HSMUN)
eligibility: High school students in a school delegation; only a teacher can register the school, up to 50 delegates per school
description: The 25th session of the U of A's high school Model UN: delegates represent countries in committee debates on global issues. Teachers register schools October 13 to November 5, 2026; students then register by December 19, 2026, and position papers are due February 12, 2027.
metaDescription: Represent a country in Model UN committees at the U of A, February 18–20, 2027. Ask a teacher to register your school.
costNote: $125 per student; fee waivers for financial hardship

name: Canadian High Schools Model United Nations (CAHSMUN)
provider: Canadian High Schools Model United Nations
eligibility: High school students registered through a school or organization delegation; no independent delegates
description: One of Canada's largest high school Model UN conferences, open to delegations from any province. A sponsor teacher registers the school first, then delegates sign up; early pricing runs to October 25 and registration closes when the conference fills. Bursaries can cover up to the full fee.
metaDescription: A national high school Model UN in Vancouver, April 2–4, 2027, with hotel included and bursaries up to the full fee.
costNote: $320 early, $360 regular, $385 late per delegate, including two nights' hotel; bursaries up to 100%

name: CalgaryHacks
provider: Computer Science Undergraduate Society, University of Calgary
grades: Ages 16+ (high school students compete in their own tier)
stipend: Prizes in a tier for high school students and first-year undergraduates
location: Calgary (University of Calgary ICT Building, in-person)
eligibility: Students aged 16 and older studying in Canada who can attend in person; high school students are placed in Tier 2 with first-year undergraduates
description: A 24-hour in-person hackathon at UCalgary where teams build a project from scratch. High school students compete in a separate prize tier with first-year university students, so you are not up against senior engineers. Free to enter; the 2027 event has not been posted yet.
metaDescription: A free 24-hour hackathon at UCalgary each February, with a prize tier for high school students aged 16 and up.

name: Canadian Student Leadership Conference (CSLC)
eligibility: Student leaders in a school delegation of up to 4 students and 2 advisors; the school must be a CSLA member
description: The national student leadership conference, held since 1985 in a different province each year. Registration fills fast: for 2026 it opened April 21 and was full the same afternoon, with a waitlist after that. Ask your student council advisor to register a delegation.
metaDescription: The national student leadership conference, four days in a different province each year. School delegations of up to four.
costNote: $500 per delegate plus a $95 annual CSLA school membership (2026)

name: Canadian Economics Olympiad (CEO)
duration: Online Round 1, then invitational national finals
eligibility: Canadian high school students; registration for 2027 opens in January 2027
description: Canada's high school economics competition and the qualifier for the International Economics Olympiad, covering economics, finance and business case analysis. Five students go to the International Economics Olympiad and five to the Economics Olympiad International Final Round. Registration for 2027 opens in January.
metaDescription: Canada's economics, finance and business-case contest for high school students, and the route to the international olympiad.

name: Canadian Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad (CAAO)
provider: Canadian Association of Amateur Astronomers (Astro Society)
duration: Take-home round of about six theory problems
location: Submitted remotely; national training camp in person for top students
eligibility: High school students in Canada, in Junior or Senior division
description: Canada's astronomy olympiad: solve around six astrophysics theory problems within a set window and send in your solutions. Top scorers go to a national training camp and a team selection test for Canada's team at the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics.
metaDescription: Six take-home astrophysics problems; top scorers train for Canada's team at the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics.

name: The Aristotle Contest – High School Philosophy Essay
provider: University of Toronto Department of Philosophy + Ontario Philosophy Teachers' Association
duration: One essay of up to 1,200 words
stipend: $500 first, $400 second, $300 third, plus up to ten honourable mentions
eligibility: Any student at a Canadian high school, at or below Grade 12, including homeschooled students; English or French
description: A philosophy essay contest for Canadian high school students: answer one of three questions in at most 1,200 words. Each essay is read blind by a high school teacher and a U of T philosophy professor. The 2026 deadline has passed; watch the page for the 2027 questions.
metaDescription: A 1,200-word philosophy essay contest for Canadian high school students, with cash prizes up to $500 from U of T.

name: Canada Service Corps
provider: Government of Canada (Employment and Social Development Canada)
duration: Flexible (at least 120 hours over 12 months) or full-time placements
location: Across Canada, including Alberta (in-person and remote)
eligibility: Young Canadians aged 15–30; placements are run by partner organizations, and some regional programs start younger
description: The federal youth volunteer service program: find a service placement with a partner organization, or propose your own project and apply for a micro-grant to run it. Placements are volunteer, not paid. Search and apply for current placements at youth.volunteer.ca.
metaDescription: Federal youth service placements for Canadians aged 15–30, or a micro-grant to run your own community project.

name: Queen's Commonwealth Writing Competition
duration: One piece of up to 1,000 words
stipend: Regional winners are invited to London for a week and an award ceremony; every entrant gets a graded certificate
location: Online (open across the Commonwealth, including Canada)
eligibility: Nationals or residents of a Commonwealth country, including Canada, aged 18 or younger on the deadline; AI-written work is disqualified
description: The world's oldest international schools writing competition, run since 1883. Write up to 1,000 words on the year's theme; one winner is chosen from each Commonwealth region, including the Americas, and every entrant receives a Gold, Silver, Bronze or Participation certificate. The 2026 deadline was April 30.
metaDescription: Write up to 1,000 words on the year's theme; the Americas winner is flown to London. Open to Canadians 18 and under.

name: NSS Gerard K. O'Neill Space Settlement Contest
duration: Design project submitted once a year
eligibility: Students up to Grade 12 from any country, as individuals, small teams of 2–5 or large teams of 6–12, each judged separately
description: Design a free-orbiting space settlement anywhere in the solar system, from structure to how people live there. More than 29,000 students from 31 countries entered in 2026. Top entrants can present at the International Space Development Conference (2027: May 27–30).
metaDescription: Design a space settlement alone or in a team; more than 29,000 students from 31 countries entered in 2026.

name: SAIT Summer Camps – Grades 9–12
duration: Week-long day camps, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm (2026: seven weeks from June 29 to August 14)
eligibility: Students in or entering Grade 9 through 12 for the high school camps; a Child and Youth Bursary Program supports families in need
description: Hands-on week-long camps at SAIT in trades and technology: welding, construction, automotive and aviation mechanics, electronics, engineering, computers and media arts, plus career-skills camps for high school students. Each week has its own registration deadline.
metaDescription: Week-long SAIT day camps for grades 9–12 in welding, mechanics, electronics and media arts, with bursaries.
costNote: Weekly fee varies by camp; bursaries for families in need

name: Lethbridge Polytechnic Dual Credit
duration: Varies by course (a semester for most)
location: Online and on campus in Lethbridge; some trades courses only at partner collegiate divisions
eligibility: Grades 10–12 students at one of 40+ partner school divisions across Alberta, including Calgary Catholic, Lethbridge and Red Deer Public; enrol through your high school
description: More than 40 dual credit courses for 2026–27 across nine areas: arts and tech, business, communication, health, human services, justice, math and engineering, sciences and trades, including an Introduction to the Trades pathway. Finishing one or more courses guarantees admission to a Lethbridge Polytechnic program (apprenticeship and competitive-entry programs excepted). Ask your guidance counsellor.
metaDescription: 40+ dual credit courses in trades, health, justice and more, with guaranteed admission to Lethbridge Polytechnic after.
costNote: Usually covered by your school division; some courses have book or supply fees

name: Red Deer Polytechnic Dual Credit
location: Mostly online (asynchronous); some programs in person in Red Deer
eligibility: Grades 10–12 students in six Central Alberta partners: Red Deer Catholic, Red Deer Public, Clearview, Wolf Creek, Chinook's Edge and Central Alberta Collegiate Institute; register through your school
description: Take Red Deer Polytechnic courses while still in high school and graduate with both credits, or even a certificate. Options include psychology, biology for health professions, sociology, personal fitness and an introduction to the construction trades. Talk to your guidance counsellor to register.
metaDescription: Central Alberta students in grades 10–12 take Red Deer Polytechnic courses for both credits, mostly online.

name: Northwestern Polytechnic Dual Credit
location: Online with optional in-person parts (Grande Prairie and region); labs or clinicals for some health courses
eligibility: Grades 11–12 students at one of 15 partner school divisions in northwestern Alberta, including Grande Prairie Public and Peace Wapiti; prerequisites vary by course
description: Dual credit in business, early learning and child care, education, health (including health care aide), humanities and skilled trades. Start with your guidance counsellor, who sends your permission package to NWP; you then apply online and hear back in three to four weeks. The $80 application fee is waived for 2026–27.
metaDescription: Dual credit in business, health, trades and more for grades 11–12 in northwestern Alberta; 2026–27 fee waived.
costNote: $80 application fee waived for 2026–27; tuition and materials set by each school division

name: Bow Valley College Dual Credit
duration: Varies by course, with flexible scheduling
location: Online and at the downtown Calgary campus
eligibility: Grades 10–12 students; eligibility depends on attendance, commitment and progress in required courses. Apply through your high school guidance counsellor
description: Eleven college courses you can take in high school for both credits: anatomy and physiology, digital design, video production, animation, esports business, medical terminology, criminal justice, sociology, legal studies and child development.
metaDescription: Eleven Bow Valley College courses for grades 10–12, from anatomy to animation, online or downtown Calgary.

name: Northern Lakes College Dual Credit
location: Northern Alberta community campuses and online
eligibility: Grades 10–12 students whose school or school division approves them; applications go through the school division
description: Twenty-three dual credit opportunities in northern Alberta: trades (carpenter, electrician, welder, heavy equipment technician), health care aide, practical nurse, primary care paramedic, business, power engineering, social work, education assistant and university studies. Bursary forms are available; start with your school.
metaDescription: 23 dual credit options in northern Alberta, from welding and power engineering to practical nursing and paramedic.

name: Canadian Cadet Program (Air, Army and Sea Cadets)
provider: Department of National Defence, with the Air, Army and Navy Leagues
duration: Year-round, weekly parade nights at a local corps or squadron
location: Local corps and squadrons across Alberta
eligibility: Canadian residents aged 12 to 18 with provincial health coverage; cadets are not members of the military and have no obligation to join
description: A free national youth program in three elements: Air Cadets (aviation, including ground school), Army Cadets and Sea Cadets, all built around leadership, fitness, marksmanship, public speaking and community service. Pick an element, find the nearest unit in the corps and squadron directory, register online, then meet local staff to finish joining.
metaDescription: Free Air, Army and Sea Cadets for ages 12–18 across Alberta: leadership, aviation and service, with no military obligation.

name: Conservation Champions Club – Calgary Zoo
duration: September to June, with monthly Saturday field trips
eligibility: Teens aged 14–17 interested in wildlife and the natural world
description: A free year-long conservation program: explore one big conservation question through expert videos and discussion online, monthly Saturday field trips and hands-on service-learning at real conservation sites, while meeting people who work in conservation careers. Ends with a certificate of completion.
metaDescription: A free September-to-June conservation program for ages 14–17, with monthly field trips and a certificate.

name: Junior Zoo Guides – Calgary Zoo
duration: One year: 60 hours in summer plus 20 hours at fall and winter events
eligibility: Ages 14–17, committing to a full year. Application windows are short and announced on the zoo's social media
description: Youth volunteers at the Calgary Zoo help with visitor engagement, summer camps, ZOOLIGHTS and Easter events (not with the animals). Apply online, then attend a group interview, orientation and training, and a 20-hour shadowing period.
metaDescription: Volunteer at the Calgary Zoo from age 14: a year of summer camps, visitor engagement and ZOOLIGHTS, 80 hours in all.

name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
duration: Several weeks each summer, starting mid-to-late June
stipend: Free for lower-income families; selected students who would otherwise need a summer job also receive $3,000
eligibility: High school students graduating in 2028 for the 2027 program; students attending school outside the US apply as international applicants, with an earlier deadline
description: A residential research summer in astrophysics (tracking a near-Earth asteroid), biochemistry, bacterial genomics or cell biology, with about 700 students a year and no grades or tests. Admission is need-blind. Applications for 2027 open around the end of December 2026; the 2026 international deadline was January 29, earlier than the US one.
metaDescription: Research a near-Earth asteroid or a protein in a residential summer program, free for lower-income families.
costNote: Free for families earning $75,000 or less, discounted under about $140,000; need-blind admission

name: Canadian Math Kangaroo Contest
duration: 75 minutes, 30 questions, on one Sunday in March
stipend: Monetary awards of $250 to $1,000 for top Grade 11 and 12 students
location: Test centres, including Mount Royal University and Renert School in Calgary, and Concordia University of Edmonton and MacEwan University in Edmonton
eligibility: Students in grades 1–12; register individually online and write at a test centre
description: A multiple-choice math contest written the same day at centres across Canada, with its own paper for grades 11–12. The 2026 contest ran Sunday, March 22, with registration closing February 23 (early-bird price to February 9). Grade 11 and 12 students with strong results over several years can earn awards of up to $1,000.
metaDescription: A 75-minute math contest in March at Calgary and Edmonton centres, with awards up to $1,000 for grades 11–12.
costNote: $20 early-bird, $25 regular per student (2026)

name: Rotary Youth Exchange – Long-Term (Alberta)
provider: Rotary District 5360 (southern Alberta) and District 5370 (northern Alberta)
duration: 10–11 months abroad, August to June or July
location: Abroad, living with 2–4 host families and attending school full-time
eligibility: Canadian citizens or permanent residents aged 15.5 to 17.9 on departure, with above-average marks and leadership, returning to high school afterwards. A local Rotary club must sponsor you; apply through your own district
description: A school year abroad as a Rotary youth ambassador: live with two to four host families, attend high school full-time and learn the language. For the August 2027 departure, southern Alberta applications close November 15, 2026, with interviews in late November. Students in northern Alberta apply through Rotary District 5370.
metaDescription: Spend a school year abroad with Rotary host families, for ages 15.5 to 17.9, sponsored by a local Rotary club.

name: Jack Chapters – Jack.org
location: High schools and campuses across Canada, including Alberta
eligibility: Youth aged 13–24; join a chapter at your school or start one with an adult ally
description: Youth-led mental health groups in more than 150 high schools, colleges and universities: members plan their own initiatives, run awareness events and advocate on the mental health issues that matter to their community. Jack.org provides training, monthly coaching calls and annual funding to chapters.
metaDescription: Join or start a youth-led mental health chapter at your high school, with training and funding from Jack.org.

name: CEMC Math Circles – Online
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
grades: Grades 9–10 online (Grades 11–12 in person at Waterloo only)
duration: Weekly 90-minute evening sessions: 8 weeks in fall (October 5 – November 26, 2026) and 8 in winter (February 8 – April 8, 2027)
eligibility: Students from Grades 6 to 12 anywhere; the online sections run up to the Grade 9/10 level
description: A free weekly math enrichment program run by Waterloo's CEMC, exploring topics beyond the curriculum through short lessons and problem solving. The Grade 9/10 online section meets Wednesday or Thursday evenings (Eastern Time, so late afternoon in Alberta). Register September 10–28, 2026.
metaDescription: Free weekly math enrichment from Waterloo for grades 9–10, live online through the fall and winter terms.

name: Girls Who Code Canada – Summer Programs
duration: 2-week live virtual Summer Immersion Program, or the 6-week self-paced Pathways course
eligibility: Students in Canada aged 14–18
description: Free virtual summer programs from Girls Who Code Canada, set up to close the gender gap in technology. The Summer Immersion Program runs two weeks of live classes, Monday to Friday, with partner events; Pathways is a self-paced six-week course in web development, cybersecurity, data science or artificial intelligence.
metaDescription: Free virtual summer coding programs for ages 14–18: two weeks of live classes, or a six-week self-paced course.

name: Alberta Aviation Museum Youth Volunteer Program
eligibility: Youth aged 13–17
description: Youth volunteers at Edmonton's aviation museum work as docents, visitor representatives and historical interpreters alongside the programming and visitor services teams: museum and public-speaking experience with a focus on aviation history.
metaDescription: Volunteer at Edmonton's aviation museum from age 13 as a docent, interpreter or visitor representative.

name: Parlement jeunesse de l'Alberta (PJA)
eligibility: French-speaking youth aged 14–25 from across Alberta; 14- and 15-year-olds start as pages
description: A French-language youth parliament held in the Alberta Legislature chamber: debate bills written by and for youth as a deputy, or take part as a page, lobbyist or journalist (the last two count toward the Leadership 15-3 course). Registration details for 2027 are not yet posted; contact FJA.
metaDescription: Debate bills in French in the Alberta Legislature chamber, April 29 to May 2, 2027, for youth aged 14–25.

name: Alberta Junior Forest Wardens
duration: Year-round club meetings, camps and trips
eligibility: Youth aged 6–17 as of October 15; families register with a local club
description: An outdoor club program in wilderness skills, forestry, ecology and leadership, with regular meetings, camps, hikes, canoe trips and skiing. The Adventurers and Challengers level includes a conference weekend and competitions that test outdoor knowledge and teamwork. Find a club near you on the association's site.
metaDescription: Outdoor clubs across Alberta in wilderness skills, forestry and ecology, with a Challengers level for ages 15–18.

name: Métis Youth Summer Employment Program
duration: 6 to 16 weeks between May and August
stipend: Paid summer job; the employer's wage is partly subsidized
eligibility: Métis youth aged 15–30 registered for full-time school in the September after the job. Register at a Métis Training to Employment Services office and meet an employment counsellor first
description: A paid summer job of 6 to 16 weeks, with Rupertsland Institute subsidizing part of the wage, for Métis students heading back to school in the fall. Call 1-888-48-MÉTIS (1-888-486-8847) to confirm the current intake and register.
metaDescription: A paid 6-to-16-week summer job for Métis students aged 15–30 returning to school, subsidized by Rupertsland Institute.

name: Centre for Health Informatics Summer Studentship – University of Calgary
provider: Centre for Health Informatics, Cumming School of Medicine, University of Calgary
duration: 8 weeks for high school students, between May and August
stipend: Stipend provided
eligibility: High school, undergraduate and graduate students from any background (arts, health sciences, kinesiology, math, science) considering a career in health data science or informatics
description: An eight-week, in-person summer placement in health data science and health informatics research, matched to a Centre for Health Informatics faculty member by your interests. The 2026 round opened December 15, 2025 and closed January 5, 2026; expect the same winter window for summer 2027.
metaDescription: Eight paid summer weeks in health data science research at UCalgary for high school students; apply each winter.

name: WISEST SET Conference – University of Alberta
provider: WISEST (Women in Scholarship, Engineering, Science and Technology), University of Alberta
duration: 1 day (2026: Saturday, November 21, 9 am to 3 pm)
eligibility: Female students in grades 10–12; dedicated spots and mentorship for Indigenous students. Capped at 225 participants
description: A one-day science, engineering and technology conference with hands-on lab activities, panels with professionals, career sessions and a networking mixer. Registration opens October 2, 2026, with payment due November 3; it is limited to 225 students, so register early to choose your sessions.
metaDescription: A one-day STEM conference at the U of A for female students in grades 10–12, with labs, panels and lunch.
costNote: $75 including lunch; lower fee without lunch

name: Wharton Global High School Investment Competition
provider: Wharton Global Youth Program, University of Pennsylvania
duration: September to December online, with a Global Finale in late April
location: Online; finals in Philadelphia (finalists can join virtually)
eligibility: High school students anywhere in teams of 4–6 with a teacher advisor from their school
description: A free team competition built on a real client case: research, build a long-term strategy in the Wharton Investment Simulator, and submit four deliverables from October to December. Teams are judged on the strategy and how well they defend it, not on portfolio returns. Registration for 2026–27 closed September 11, 2026; the next season opens each August.
metaDescription: A free team investing case competition from Wharton, judged on strategy, not returns. Registration opens each August.

name: Diamond Challenge – High School Entrepreneurship
duration: September to April: concept submission, pitch rounds, and a summit for finalists
stipend: Grand prizes of $12,000, $8,000 and $4,500 in each track, from a $100,000+ prize pool
location: Online, with an in-person summit for finalists (2027: April 29–30)
eligibility: Teams of 2–4 high school students aged 14–18 on the deadline, from any country, with an adult advisor aged 21 or older
description: A free global pitch competition in two tracks: Business Innovation (a venture that makes money solving a customer problem) and Social Innovation (a venture with social or environmental impact). Submit a 3–5 page concept and a 60-second video; advancing teams hear back February 10, and finalists pitch at the summit.
metaDescription: A free global pitch competition for teams aged 14–18, in business or social innovation, with top prizes of $12,000.

name: Purple Comet! Math Meet
duration: 90 minutes, 30 problems, started any time in a ten-day window in April
eligibility: Teams of 1–6 students from any country; an adult supervisor registers the team
description: A free online team math contest held every year since 2003: pick a start time in the ten-day window and solve 30 problems ranging from easy to extremely hard. In 2025, more than 12,000 students on 4,000 teams from 80 countries took part.
metaDescription: A free online team math contest each April: 30 problems in 90 minutes, with teams of up to six from 80 countries.

name: picoCTF – Carnegie Mellon Cybersecurity Competition
duration: 10-day competition each spring (2026: March 9–19); practice platform open all year
eligibility: Students worldwide aged 13 and up; under 18 needs parental consent
description: A free capture-the-flag hacking competition from Carnegie Mellon: solve security puzzles in cryptography, web exploitation, forensics and reverse engineering. The picoGym practice site runs year-round with past challenges and guided lessons, so you can start well before the spring competition.
metaDescription: A free capture-the-flag cybersecurity competition from Carnegie Mellon each spring, with a practice site open all year.

name: John Locke Institute Global Essay Prize
duration: One essay of up to 2,000 words
stipend: Per category: $5,000, $2,000 and $1,000 scholarships; a $10,000 Junior Fellowship grand prize
location: Online (open worldwide); awards ceremony in London
eligibility: Students of any age under 19 on the submission deadline, from any country
description: An international essay prize in ten subjects: economics, history, international relations, law, philosophy, politics, psychology, public policy, science and technology, and theology, with three questions each. The 2026 cycle opened registration February 2, closed it March 31, and took essays until May 31. Free at the standard deadline.
metaDescription: A free international essay prize in ten subjects, from economics to philosophy, with scholarships up to $10,000.
costNote: Free by the standard deadline; late entries cost extra

name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
duration: Submit work each fall; regional then national judging
stipend: Recognition and scholarships at the national level
eligibility: Students in grades 7–12, aged 13 or older, living in Canada outside Quebec or in the US; fee waivers available
description: The long-running North American awards for teen art and writing, with more than 100,000 entries a year across art and writing categories. The 2027 Awards open October 1, 2026, with regional deadlines from early December to early January; Canadian students are placed in an art region and a writing region by their postal code.
metaDescription: Enter your art or writing in North America's big teen awards, open to Canadians outside Quebec in grades 7–12.
costNote: $15 per individual entry, $40 per portfolio; fee waivers available

name: Blue Planet Awareness Contest (Bow Seat)
provider: Bow Seat Creative Action for Conservation
stipend: Cash awards up to $1,000, plus exhibition and publication opportunities
eligibility: Students aged 11–18 anywhere, not yet in college, as individuals or groups; an adult sponsor is required
description: Formerly the Ocean Awareness Contest: respond to the year's environmental theme with art, film, poetry, creative writing, music, dance or interactive work. The 2027 theme is "Nature of Truth: Environmentalism in an Age of Disinformation".
metaDescription: Answer an environmental theme with art, writing, film or music, ages 11–18 worldwide, for awards up to $1,000.

name: The Earth Prize
duration: Registration to January 10, blueprint submission by January 31
stipend: Seven regional winners get $10,000 each; $104,500 in total prizes
eligibility: Students born between 2007 and 2014 in school or homeschool, alone or in teams of up to five from any school
description: The world's largest environmental sustainability competition for teenagers: identify a real environmental problem and design a solution, submitted as an Earth Prize Blueprint that ends in a video pitch. Register by January 10, 2027 and submit by January 31, 2027.
metaDescription: Design a solution to a real environmental problem, alone or in a team of five, for $10,000 regional prizes.

name: Green Certificate Program
duration: Varies by specialization; runs alongside high school
location: On farms and agricultural operations across Alberta
eligibility: Alberta high school students aged 15 or older in Grade 10 or above; apply through your school's off-campus education coordinator
description: An apprenticeship-style agriculture program: train on-site under experienced farm staff in one of 13 pathways, from beef, dairy and equine to field crops, greenhouse, poultry, sheep and swine. Earn up to 16 Grade 12 diploma credits and a credential toward a career in agriculture. Enrolment is year-round.
metaDescription: Train on a farm in one of 13 agriculture pathways and earn up to 16 Grade 12 credits, from age 15 in Grade 10.

name: Youth Agriculture Speaking Championships – Calgary Stampede
provider: Calgary Stampede, with Olds College and the Alberta Association of Agricultural Societies
duration: 5–7 minute speech; preliminaries in late June and July, finals at the Stampede
stipend: Up to $2,000 for first in the Senior final ($1,000 Junior); $150–$200 at preliminaries; winners go to the national final in Toronto
location: Preliminaries at Athabasca University, Olds College and Stampede Park; finals at Stampede Park, Calgary
eligibility: Youth aged 11–24 as of November 7; no farm or agriculture background needed
description: Give a 5–7 minute speech on one of five agriculture, agri-tech or agri-food topics set each year. In 2026, entries ran February 5 to June 19, preliminaries were held June 27 and July 10, and the top four from each division advanced to the July 11 final at the Stampede, with a travel credit to the national final.
metaDescription: Give a 5–7 minute agriculture speech at the Calgary Stampede, ages 11–24, for prizes of up to $2,000 each summer.

name: University of Alberta Programming Contest (UAPC) – High School Division
stipend: $300 for first and $150 for second in the high school division (in-person teams only)
location: Edmonton (U of A, Donadeo Innovation Centre for Engineering); remote entry allowed but not eligible for prizes
eligibility: Teams of 1–3 students who are all still in school (below university); registration by Google Form, and spots are limited
description: A free programming contest with a dedicated high school division: mostly approachable problems with a few harder ones, solved in C++, Python, Java, C, Kotlin, Rust or Haskell. Lunch is provided on site. The 2026 contest ran March 7, with registration closing two days before.
metaDescription: A free programming contest at the U of A each March with its own high school division and cash prizes.

name: Calgary Collegiate Programming Contest (CCPC)
provider: Competitive Programming Club, University of Calgary
duration: One Saturday in March, 10 am to 6 pm (2026: March 28)
eligibility: Teams of up to three students enrolled at a Calgary high school or post-secondary institution; Division 2 is for those who have not won cash prizes at CCPC or ACPC
description: A free team programming contest run by UCalgary's Competitive Programming Club, open to Calgary high school students as well as university students, with a second division for newer competitors. The organizer's event page records the March 28, 2026 contest and its rules. That event has ended; the next contest date has not been announced.
metaDescription: A free team programming contest at UCalgary each March, open to Calgary high school students; it often sells out.

name: National Youth Remembrance Contests – Royal Canadian Legion
grades: Kindergarten to Grade 12 (senior category for high school)
stipend: Cash prizes at the national level; first-place senior winners go to Ottawa for the National Remembrance Day Ceremony
location: Through your local Legion branch; video entries online
eligibility: Students across Canada; poster and literary entries go to your nearest Legion branch, which sets its own deadline
description: Remembrance-themed contests in three forms: a poster, an original essay or poem, or a video. Poster and literary entries are judged at the branch, then provincial, then national level; video entries go online from September 1 to December 15, 2026. Ask your nearest Legion branch for its poster and literary deadline.
metaDescription: Enter a Remembrance poster, essay, poem or video; the top senior winners represent Canadian youth in Ottawa.

name: Poetry In Voice – National Recitation Competition
provider: Poetry In Voice / Les voix de la poésie
duration: Online qualifier in February and March, national finals in April
stipend: Cash and travel prizes; Senior finalists go to the National Finals in Toronto
location: Online qualifiers; Senior National Finals in Toronto (2027: April 17–21)
eligibility: Students attending a school in Canada, 18 or younger for Senior; homeschooled students compete through a participating school. A signed permission form is required
description: Memorize and recite poems from the Poetry In Voice anthology, including at least one written before the 21st century, in the English, French or bilingual stream. Submissions open February 1, 2027; senior semifinalists are named March 11 and finalists March 18.
metaDescription: Recite poems in English, French or both for cash and a trip to the Toronto finals, open to grades 10–12.

name: Venturer Scouts – Scouts Canada
duration: School year, weekly meetings plus expeditions
eligibility: Youth aged 15–17; anyone can join at any time of year, with financial assistance available
description: The Scouts Canada section for ages 15–17: youth plan and lead their own outdoor expeditions, service projects and leadership challenges with others who share their interests. Fees combine the national membership fee and a local group fee; Scouts Canada offers financial assistance so cost is not a barrier.
metaDescription: Plan and lead outdoor expeditions and service projects with Venturer Scouts, ages 15–17, across Alberta.
costNote: National membership fee plus a local group fee; financial assistance available

name: Rangers – Girl Guides of Canada
duration: School year, meeting weekly or every other week
eligibility: Girls aged 15–17; register online and pick a unit near you with the unit finder
description: The Girl Guides branch for teens: Rangers lead community projects, mentor younger girls, raise awareness for causes they choose, and go on overnight canoe trips while learning skills like budgeting and resume writing. Registration for 2026–27 is open.
metaDescription: Lead community projects, mentor younger girls and go canoe tripping with Girl Guides Rangers, ages 15–17.
costNote: Under $200 a year for weekly programming, plus uniform and some activity costs

name: YSC Virtual Regional STEM Fair
duration: Year-long project; virtual fair in spring
eligibility: Students in grades 7–12 anywhere in Canada whose community has no regional STEM fair, or whose regional fair is not running that year
description: Youth Science Canada's online regional fair for students with no regional fair near them, which covers much of rural Alberta outside the seven regional fairs. Present a science or engineering project virtually, the same way regional fairs lead toward the Canada-Wide Science Fair.
metaDescription: A virtual science fair for Canadian students in grades 7–12 with no regional fair nearby, including rural Alberta.

name: Experiences Canada Group Exchanges
provider: Experiences Canada (funded by the Government of Canada)
duration: 7–10 days per visit, hosting and travelling (reciprocal homestays)
stipend: Group travel costs covered
location: Anywhere in Canada (reciprocal, with a twinned group)
eligibility: Groups of 10–60 youth aged 12–17 with chaperones; a teacher, coach, choir director or community leader organizes and applies for the group
description: A funded homestay exchange between your group and a twinned group elsewhere in Canada: each group hosts the other for 7–10 days. Themes include sports, music, Indigenous, regional, language and history exchanges. Organizers apply year-round, at least 60 days before travel.
metaDescription: A funded homestay exchange between your school or club group and one elsewhere in Canada, ages 12–17.
costNote: $250 membership per group and $250 registration per participant; travel covered

name: Alberta Youth Leaders for Environmental Education (AYLEE)
duration: School year, virtual meetings every second Wednesday, 5:30–7 pm
eligibility: Alberta students in grades 9–12; apply any time in the school year (earlier is better)
description: A free province-wide youth group on environment, energy and climate: meet online every two weeks, lead your own AYLEE Action Project in your community, and present at environmental and education events, with chances to work on advocacy campaigns, white papers and youth summits.
metaDescription: A free online youth group for Alberta students in grades 9–12 who lead their own environment or climate project.

name: Youth Conservation Collective – CPAWS Southern Alberta
duration: About three months: an August bootcamp, five Saturday field days in the fall, and a December showcase
eligibility: Students entering Grade 10, 11 or 12 who can attend the bootcamp, the showcase and at least three field days
description: Work on a conservation action project with a mentor, do field studies with professionals and present your work at a showcase. The 2026 cohort's applications opened April 1, with a bootcamp August 22–23 and a showcase December 5; expect the next intake to open in spring 2027.
metaDescription: A three-month conservation program near Calgary for grades 10–12: field days, a mentor, and your own action project.

name: UBC Future Global Leaders
duration: Summer courses and mini schools in July and August
location: UBC Vancouver campus (residential option) or online
eligibility: Ages 15–18 with Grade 10 finished (about a 78% average recommended). No application or transcript: check eligibility and register
description: First-year-level summer courses and mini schools taught by UBC instructors, without exams, in areas like business and economics, engineering and technology, health and life sciences, media and fine arts, history, law and politics. On-campus students add workshops and social activities; everyone gets a letter of completion.
metaDescription: Take a first-year-level summer course at UBC, on campus or online, for ages 15–18 who have finished Grade 10.
costNote: Course or mini-school fee, plus residence for on-campus students

name: Hack Club
stipend: Up to $100 starter funding for a new club, plus project-based hardware grants
location: Your own school (student-led), with an online community
eligibility: High school students anywhere; start a new club or convert an existing one at your school
description: A worldwide network of student-led high school coding clubs where members learn by building and shipping a project at each meeting. Everything is free: leadership training, curriculum, an online community, a web-based coding environment, and "You ship, we ship" programs that reward finished projects with hardware.
metaDescription: Start or join a free student-led coding club at your school, with curriculum, starter funding and hardware grants.

name: The Concord Review
duration: Self-paced; one research essay of 5,000 to 10,000 words or more
location: Online submission, open to secondary students anywhere
eligibility: Secondary school students anywhere who wrote the paper alone before finishing high school; not previously published outside a school publication
description: A quarterly journal that publishes history research papers written by secondary students. Essays run 5,000 to 10,000 words or more with Chicago-style endnotes, and about 5% of submissions are published. Papers are accepted on a rolling basis and stay eligible for the next three issues (quarterly cutoffs are August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1).
metaDescription: Submit a long history research paper to a quarterly journal that publishes secondary students' work from anywhere.
costNote: Submission fee from US$70 (eBook edition), which includes a one-year subscription

name: Journal of Emerging Investigators (JEI)
duration: Self-paced; peer review and revision typically take several months
eligibility: Middle and high school students aged 13 or older, with an adult senior author (teacher, professor, graduate student, or parent for home research). The adult submits the manuscript
description: A peer-reviewed science journal run by graduate students that publishes original research by middle and high school students. Every manuscript needs a student author and an adult senior author, and editors and reviewers give detailed feedback that guides the paper through revision to publication. Submissions are accepted year-round.
metaDescription: Publish your own science research in a peer-reviewed journal for students 13 and up, with feedback from scientists.
costNote: US$49 per submission; a limited number of need-based fee scholarships each year

name: HiMCM – High School Mathematical Contest in Modeling
provider: COMAP (Consortium for Mathematics and Its Applications)
eligibility: High school students (or younger) anywhere, in teams of up to four with a faculty advisor; no limit on teams per school
description: An international team contest where high school students pick one of several open-ended real-world problems, build a mathematical model and write up their solution as a report. Teams have 14 consecutive days in the contest window to download the problem, work on it and submit electronically, under a teacher advisor.
metaDescription: Team up with up to three classmates to solve a real-world problem with a math model and a written report over 14 days.

name: Cubes in Space
duration: Design over the school year; launches in summer 2027
location: Online program; experiments ship to Virginia to fly on NASA missions
eligibility: Students aged 11 to 18 not in college or university, with an adult educator (teacher, club leader, homeschool parent) who registers and delivers the program. Students outside the US fly on balloon missions only
description: Students design an experiment small enough to fit in a 4 cm or 10 cm cube and propose it for flight. Selected experiments fly on a NASA sounding rocket or scientific balloon and come back for analysis. Registration for the 2027 missions opens November 9, 2026; students from outside the US can fly on the balloon missions.
metaDescription: Design a small experiment that could fly on a NASA scientific balloon, for ages 11 to 18 working with an adult educator.
costNote: Free to register and apply; a US$75 flight fee if selected, plus shipping both ways for international teams

name: Wolfram High School Summer Research Program
duration: About two and a half weeks in late June and July
eligibility: High school students with a background in any STEM subject who will be under 18 at the end of the program; international students accepted
description: An intensive residential program where about 80 high school students learn Wolfram Language and computational thinking, then complete an original research project with a mentor. Applications for 2026 closed in March; the 2027 dates and deadlines have not been posted yet. Admission is need-blind.
metaDescription: Spend summer near Boston doing a computational research project with a mentor, for high school students under 18.
costNote: About US$5,500 including room and board in 2026; need-based scholarships available

name: GENIUS Olympiad
provider: GENIUS Olympiad, hosted at St. John Fisher University
location: Finals in person in Rochester, New York
eligibility: Students in grades 8 to 12 from any country, with a project in one of nine categories
description: An international high school project fair with nine categories: science, art, short film, music, robotics, entrepreneurship, speech, coding and artificial intelligence. Students submit a project online; finalists are announced March 25 and present in person at the finals in Rochester, New York.
metaDescription: Enter a science, art, film, music, robotics or coding project in an international fair with finals in New York.
costNote: US$75 application fee per project; US$695 per finalist to take part in the finals

name: European Astro Pi Challenge – Mission Space Lab
provider: European Space Agency and the Raspberry Pi Foundation
duration: Registration September 14, 2026 to February 22, 2027; about 2 to 6 hours of work
location: Online; code runs on computers aboard the International Space Station
eligibility: Young people under 19 in ESA member states and cooperating states, including Canada, working alone or in teams with an adult mentor
description: Students write Python code for a task set by ESA scientists, test it on the Astro Pi replica, and qualifying programs run on the Astro Pi computers aboard the International Space Station. Canada takes part as an ESA cooperating state. A shorter Mission Zero, about an hour of coding, is also open.
metaDescription: Write Python that runs on a computer aboard the International Space Station, free for Canadians under 19.

name: Canadian Improv Games – Alberta
provider: Canadian Improv Games, run in Alberta by Rapid Fire Theatre
duration: Weekly practice September to March; Alberta tournament February 9–14, 2027
location: Alberta regional tournament; national festival in Ottawa, March 23–27, 2027
eligibility: High school teams of up to eight students with a teacher-coach at their own school; any student can join
description: A national improv theatre program for high school teams. Teams of up to eight practise through the school year with trainer support, compete at one of 15 regional tournaments, and top teams go to the national festival in Ottawa. In Alberta the tournament is run by Rapid Fire Theatre, which handles registration.
metaDescription: Form an improv team of up to eight at your school, train all year and compete at the Alberta tournament in February.

name: AwesomeMath Summer Program
duration: Three-week online sessions from June to August
eligibility: Middle and high school students aged 12 to 18 anywhere; apply with a math teacher recommendation and an untimed admission test
description: Live online problem-solving courses for strong math students, with a 90-minute lecture and an hour of problem solving each weekday for three weeks. Students choose from three sessions and can take one, two or all three. The 2027 application rounds have not opened; earlier rounds cost less and get better course choice.
metaDescription: Take a live three-week online problem-solving course in olympiad-style math, for students aged 12 to 18.
costNote: US$1,275 to $1,575 per course in 2026, rising with each application round

name: Interact Clubs – Rotary
provider: Rotary International, sponsored by local Rotary clubs (Districts 5360 and 5370 in Alberta)
location: Clubs at high schools across Alberta; start one at yours with a local Rotary club
eligibility: Young people aged 12 to 18; join your school's Interact club or start one with a sponsoring Rotary club
description: Rotary's service and leadership clubs for teens. Members plan local and international service projects, run fundraisers and build leadership skills with support from a sponsoring Rotary club. Northern Alberta's District 5370 alone has about 18 high school clubs, and southern Alberta's District 5360 sponsors more.
metaDescription: Join or start a Rotary Interact club at your high school to run service projects with support from local Rotarians.

name: International Youth Math Challenge (IYMC)
duration: Three online rounds through the fall
eligibility: Middle school, high school and university students worldwide, in Junior (Grade 10 or below), Youth (Grades 11 to 13) and Senior categories
description: A free online math competition in three rounds: a qualification round, a pre-final round and a final. Problems test creative problem solving rather than advanced curriculum, and there are separate categories for younger high school students, senior high school students and adults, with certificates and over US$1,500 in prizes.
metaDescription: Enter a free three-round online math contest with separate categories for younger and senior students.
costNote: Qualification round free; a 15 euro fee applies only to students who reach the pre-final round

name: Lumiere Research Scholar Program
eligibility: High school students anywhere; apply for one of several cohorts each year
description: A paid online research mentorship where each student works one-on-one with a PhD mentor to learn about a field and produce an independent research paper. Cohorts start several times a year with separate deadlines, and finishing earns credit from UC San Diego Extended Studies. It has given over US$1.8 million in financial aid to low-income students.
metaDescription: Write an independent research paper one-on-one with a PhD mentor online, in cohorts that start through the year.
costNote: Tuition charged; need-based financial aid for low-income students

name: Harvard Summer School Secondary School Program
duration: Four-week or seven-week sessions, June to August 2027
location: Residential at Harvard in Cambridge, Massachusetts, commuting, or online
eligibility: Students at least 16 by June 13, 2027 who will not turn 19 before July 31, 2027, graduating high school in 2027, 2028 or 2029; international students accepted
description: High school students take college courses for credit alongside Harvard Summer School students, in four- or seven-week sessions on campus, commuting or online. Early and regular deadlines are January 13 and February 10, 2027, and the late deadline is March 31. International residential students get visa sponsorship.
metaDescription: Take college courses for credit at Harvard for four or seven weeks, on campus or online, for students 16 to 18.
costNote: 2027 tuition from about US$4,180 (online) to US$15,980 (seven weeks residential), plus a US$75 application fee

name: Canadian Severe Storms Laboratory Internship – Western University
provider: Canadian Severe Storms Laboratory (CSSL), Western University
duration: About 8 weeks for high school interns (July 6 to August 28 in 2026)
stipend: $10,000 scholarship, non-taxable
location: Olds, AB (hail fieldwork) or London, ON
eligibility: Grade 11 and 12 students, still enrolled in school in the fall; high school hail positions go to students from Olds, AB, and other high school places to students from London, ON. Canadian citizens and permanent residents
description: A paid summer on Western University's severe storms team. The hail internship is based in Olds, Alberta and chases hailstorms to collect data; flights and housing in Olds are covered. High school interns get the same $10,000 as university interns. The 2026 round opened December 1, 2025 and closed January 26, 2026, with a required virtual info session in January.
metaDescription: Chase Alberta hailstorms for Western University's storm lab: $10,000 for Grade 11 and 12 students from Olds.

name: Focused Ultrasound High School Summer Research Program – Sunnybrook
duration: Full time through July and August
stipend: Paid position (amount not posted)
location: Toronto, ON (in-person, Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre)
eligibility: Students in grades 10 to 12 who are 16 by July 1 and legally able to work in Canada; students from outside Toronto are welcome but arrange their own housing
description: A paid summer in Sunnybrook's focused ultrasound labs in Toronto, helping with engineering, experiments and programming for medical devices that treat the body with sound. Students from outside Toronto can apply if they can work in Canada and find their own place to stay. The 2026 deadline was February 20, with a cover letter, resume, transcript and teacher evaluation.
metaDescription: Paid summer research in Sunnybrook's focused ultrasound labs in Toronto for students 16 and up, open to Albertans.

name: SickKids Summer Research Program (SSuRe)
provider: The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) Research Institute
duration: Up to 15 weeks, May to mid-August
stipend: Minimum wage plus 6% vacation pay
location: Toronto, ON (in-person; remote work only from inside Ontario)
eligibility: Graduating Grade 12 students starting a university or college program in the fall, working on a project with a SickKids Research Institute supervisor
description: A paid summer research job at SickKids in Toronto, open to students in their last year of high school who start post-secondary in the fall. You work on a project under a SickKids researcher, who must supervise you, and present at the August symposium. If you have not heard back by early April, the position has likely been filled.
metaDescription: Paid summer research at SickKids in Toronto for graduating Grade 12 students headed to university in the fall.

name: Students on the Beamlines – Canadian Light Source
duration: A school-year project with beamtime in Saskatoon
location: Your school, plus beamtime at the Canadian Light Source in Saskatoon, SK
eligibility: High school students 14 and older, as a group led by a teacher; the teacher writes the proposal and needs a prior connection with CLS Education. Grades are not a criterion
description: A teacher and a group of students design their own experiment and run it on a beamline at Canada's synchrotron in Saskatoon, then present what they found. Students lead the project with mentors from the Light Source. The teacher applies, not the student, so show this to a science teacher. The spring 2026 call closed April 1, and the next call opens in October 2026.
metaDescription: Run your own experiment on Canada's synchrotron in Saskatoon with a teacher-led group of high school students.

name: STEM Fellowship Journal
