eligibility: High school and undergraduate students anywhere, alone or in teams, in any STEM field and the related social sciences
description: A Canadian peer-reviewed, open-access journal for research by high school and university students. Papers go through double-blind review by subject experts before publication. Original research, reviews and shorter viewpoint pieces are accepted any time. Publishing costs $400 CAD once a paper is accepted, with discounts or waivers for some competition winners.
metaDescription: Publish your research in a Canadian peer-reviewed journal for high school and university students, any STEM field.
costNote: $400 CAD publication fee on acceptance; waivers for some competition winners

name: Indigenous Summer Research Academy (InSRA) – University of Lethbridge
stipend: $3,000 award for finishing, plus a $500 travel bursary
eligibility: Indigenous students who have completed Grade 11, with Math 20-1 or 20-2 and a science, a 65% average and steady attendance; priority to students from Piikani, Kainai and Siksika
description: Six weeks of hands-on research at the University of Lethbridge for Indigenous students after Grade 11, in areas from Indigenous Studies and art to genetics, neuroscience and bioengineering, ending in a poster presentation. It runs alongside the HYRS program on campus. Apply with a short essay and a reference from a teacher or community member. The 2024 program ran July 5 to August 16; newer dates are not posted yet.
metaDescription: Six paid weeks of research at the University of Lethbridge for Indigenous students after Grade 11, with a $3,000 award.

name: Young Ornithologist Workshop – Beaverhill Bird Observatory
location: Beaverhill Natural Area, east of Edmonton (camping at the station)
eligibility: Young people aged 15 to 18 with an interest in birds
description: A free week of field ornithology at an Alberta bird observatory: bird banding, identification, aging and sexing birds, migration monitoring and MAPS survey work, plus bats and butterflies. Food, field trips and instruction are covered; you get yourself to the station and bring a tent and sleeping bag (tents can be borrowed). In 2026 the workshop ran August 8 to 14 and applications closed April 30.
metaDescription: A free week of bird banding and migration monitoring at an Alberta bird observatory for ages 15 to 18, food included.

name: Science Mentorship Institute (sci-MI)
eligibility: High school students anywhere; no research experience needed
description: A free online summer research program where high school students work on a real project with a university mentor, in neuroscience, biology, computer science, electrical engineering or chemistry. It uses open data and published papers, so no lab is needed, and ends with students presenting what they found. Student applications for 2026 are closed; apply again for next summer.
metaDescription: A free online summer research project with a university mentor, in neuroscience, biology, computing, engineering or chemistry.

name: Student Advancement Research (StAR) Program – SickKids
stipend: Paid internship (amount not posted)
eligibility: Black, Filipino or Indigenous students in Grade 11 or 12, 16 by the start date, with Grade 10 Science done; Canadian citizens or permanent residents with a SIN who can be in their lab in person every day
description: A paid six-week summer internship in a SickKids research lab in Toronto for Black, Filipino and Indigenous high school students. Biology and chemistry help but are not required. You need to be at the lab in person every day. The 2026 program ran July 6 to August 14 and applications have closed; check the Kids Science page for the next round.
metaDescription: A paid six-week summer internship in a SickKids research lab in Toronto for Black, Filipino and Indigenous students in Grade 11 or 12.

name: Research Mentorship Program – UC Santa Barbara
location: Santa Barbara, California (in-person; three virtual days to start)
eligibility: High school students in Grade 10 or 11 from anywhere, with a strong academic record (a 3.80 weighted GPA in US terms); no English test needed for international applicants
description: A seven-week summer at UC Santa Barbara where you are paired with a graduate student, postdoc or professor and carry out your own research project, with lectures on research methods along the way. International students are welcome. Applications for 2027 open December 15, 2026 and close March 8, 2027, with decisions on a rolling basis. It is expensive: in 2026, US$5,675 to commute or US$13,274 living on campus.
metaDescription: Seven weeks of mentored research at UC Santa Barbara for Grade 10 and 11 students from anywhere, Canada included.
costNote: US$5,675 commuter or US$13,274 residential (2026); limited need-based aid, California residents first

name: Scihigh Summer Internship – Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute
duration: 8 weeks full time (June 29 to August 21 in 2026)
stipend: Paid position (amount not posted)
location: Toronto, ON (in-person, Mount Sinai or Hennick Bridgepoint Hospital)
eligibility: Grade 11 and 12 students who are 16 by the start, have taken or are taking Grade 11 Biology and Chemistry, can legally work in Canada and meet the hospital's immunization policy
description: A paid eight-week summer internship working full time with a biomedical research group at the Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute in Toronto. The page sets no rule on where you live, but the work is in person at Mount Sinai or Hennick Bridgepoint Hospital. Places are very competitive. Applications for summer 2026 have closed; a one-week March Break placement also runs.
metaDescription: A paid eight-week summer internship in a Toronto biomedical research lab for Grade 11 and 12 students who are 16 or older.

name: Math Mentorship Program – University of Toronto
provider: Department of Mathematics, University of Toronto
duration: January to May, meeting a mentor once or twice a month
location: Online meetings, plus two required events at U of T's St. George campus in Toronto
eligibility: High school students interested in mathematical research; the opening reception in January and the closing showcase in May are in person in Toronto and required
description: You are paired with a U of T math graduate student, postdoc or professor and work on a research project in a field of math you choose, from January to May. Meetings can be online, but the January reception and the May showcase happen in person in Toronto, so an Alberta student needs two trips. The top projects are presented at the Canadian Undergraduate Mathematics Conference. Applications open November 3 and close December 1, 2026.
metaDescription: Do a math research project with a University of Toronto mentor from January to May, with online meetings allowed.
costNote: $367.25 plus a 4.5% service fee

name: Summer of Science – McDonald Institute, Queen's University
provider: Arthur B. McDonald Canadian Astroparticle Physics Research Institute, Queen's University
grades: Middle and high school (graduating students too)
duration: 12 afternoon sessions over 4 weeks in July and August
location: Online, or in person in Kingston, ON
eligibility: Middle and high school students, including those graduating in June; students outside the Kingston area join the online group
description: A free summer program in the physical sciences run by Queen's University's astroparticle physics institute, with an online group for students outside Kingston. Over twelve afternoons you practise asking questions, forming hypotheses, experimenting and analysing data in astronomy, chemistry and particle physics, and students can join their instructors' research projects before presenting at the end. Sessions run 1:30 to 4:30 PM Eastern, which is 11:30 to 2:30 in Alberta. Apply with a one-page letter and a teacher's letter of support; the 2026 deadline was in May.
metaDescription: A free summer science program from Queen's University's physics institute, online for students outside Kingston.

name: Toshiba/NSTA ExploraVision
provider: Toshiba and the National Science Teaching Association (NSTA)
duration: Team project over the fall and winter; entries close January 27, 2027
location: Online entry; national finalists travel to Washington, DC
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 4 students who are Canadian or US citizens living in Canada or the US, in school full time and 21 or younger, with a coach aged 21+ (a teacher, counsellor, youth leader or parent)
description: A science competition for Canadian and US students. Your team of 2 to 4 imagines a future technology, researches the science behind it and writes it up: a project description of up to 11 pages, an abstract, a bibliography and a launch flyer. High school teams (Grades 10 to 12) compete in their own division. First-prize students each get US$5,000 cash (or a larger savings bond), second prize US$2,500, and the eight finalist teams go to Washington, DC in June. Every student on a team that submits a complete project gets a certificate and a gift. Note that it asks for citizenship, not residency.
metaDescription: Team up with 2 to 4 classmates, design a future technology and compete for up to US$5,000 each plus a DC trip.

name: Bold Eagle – Canadian Armed Forces
duration: About 6 weeks, early July to late August
stipend: Paid for the whole program; travel, food, lodging and gear are covered
eligibility: First Nations (Status or non-Status), Métis or Inuit youth who are Canadian citizens, 16 or older with Grade 10 done (parent consent under 18), from Western Canada: Thunder Bay to the West Coast, including the territories
description: A paid summer program at CFB Wainwright for Indigenous youth from Western Canada that combines basic military training with cultural teachings led by Elders. You learn drill, navigation, first aid and weapons handling, and finish with the Army Reserve Basic Military Qualification. After it you can stay in the Forces or be released, and some high schools count the time as career experience credits. The Forces pay you and cover travel, food and lodging. Applications usually close at the end of April. The 2026 course, its 37th year, graduated 64 people.
metaDescription: A paid six-week summer at CFB Wainwright for Indigenous youth 16+, mixing basic military training with Elder-led teachings.

name: National Youth Orchestra of Canada (NYO Canada)
duration: About 7 weeks, mid-June to early August 2027
stipend: Full scholarship plus an honorarium
eligibility: Orchestral musicians aged 16 to 28 on July 1, 2027 who live in Canada, including full-time students at a Canadian school; video audition
description: Canada's national training orchestra. Musicians spend the summer in intensive rehearsal and coaching with professional faculty, then perform. No member pays tuition: everyone gets a full scholarship and an honorarium. You apply with an audition video. The application fee rises the later you apply: $50 in the first week of October, $75 to November 30 and $100 after that. Videos are due February 1, 2027.
metaDescription: Spend the summer in Canada's national youth orchestra for free, with an honorarium, if you are 16 or older.
costNote: Application fee $50 (October 1 to 7), $75 (to November 30) or $100 (to February 1); no tuition

name: Calgary Youth Orchestra
eligibility: String, wind, brass and percussion players aged 14 to 24 at about Royal Conservatory Grade 9 level or higher; everyone, returning members included, auditions in person each year
description: Calgary's senior youth orchestra, run by the Mount Royal University Conservatory. Auditions are held once a year, in person in late May and June, and adjudicated by the music director. New players bring two contrasting pieces plus scales, and returning players also prepare orchestral excerpts. Private lessons are strongly recommended. The 2026-27 season has no harp part.
metaDescription: Audition in person each spring to play a full season in Calgary's senior youth orchestra, run by Mount Royal University.

name: Edmonton Youth Orchestra
eligibility: Intermediate Orchestra for players typically 11 to 16; Senior Orchestra for advanced high school and post-secondary players up to 24; video audition (percussion may audition in person)
description: Edmonton's youth orchestra has two ensembles, Intermediate and Senior, placed by skill. You audition by video with a 2 to 5 minute piece with contrasting sections, uploaded as an unlisted YouTube video; no accompanist needed. For the 2026-27 season submissions closed May 29, 2026 with results by the end of June. Members pay a membership fee by the first September rehearsal, and scholarships and bursaries are available.
metaDescription: Audition by video for Edmonton's Intermediate or Senior youth orchestra and rehearse with it from September to spring.
costNote: Membership fee due by the first rehearsal (amount not posted); scholarships and bursaries available

name: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS)
location: Cornell University (Ithaca, NY) or University of Maryland (College Park, MD)
eligibility: Students outside the US without a US passport must apply in Grade 10 and be 15 to 17 during the program; they must be comfortable with advanced reading, writing and discussion in English
description: A free five-week humanities seminar in the US: university-level reading, writing and discussion with a small group. There are two tracks, TASS-CBS and TASS-AOS, and you apply to one. Telluride covers tuition, books, room and board and field trips, but does not help with visas. International students, Canadians included, can only apply in Grade 10. The 2026 deadline was December 3, 2025, so expect the next one in early December.
metaDescription: A free five-week university-level humanities seminar at Cornell or Maryland; Canadian students apply in Grade 10.

name: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow – Canada
duration: Entries in January and February; winners announced in May
eligibility: Groups of 1 to 50 students in Grades 6 to 12 at a publicly funded school anywhere in Canada, entered by a full-time teacher who is 21 or older
description: A national STEM contest where a class or club uses science and technology to tackle a problem in its own community. Your teacher enters by answering three short questions: the local challenge, your STEM solution, and how it will last. Finalists build out their projects. Prizes are Samsung technology vouchers for the school, up to $50,000 for first place. The 2026 entry window was January 12 to February 27.
metaDescription: Ask a teacher to enter your class or club in Samsung's national STEM contest; the school can win up to $50,000 in tech.

name: Online Physics Olympiad (OPhO)
eligibility: Teams of up to three high school or undergraduate students, from any country
description: A free, student-run team physics competition with olympiad-level problems. Since 2020 it has drawn more than 10,000 competitors from over 80 countries. The 2026 contest was one round over a weekend, with short-answer, long-answer and simulation experiment problems. Past papers, solutions and standings are posted on the site, which makes it good practice for the Canadian Physics Olympiad.
metaDescription: Enter a free online physics olympiad with up to two friends: one weekend of olympiad problems, open worldwide.

name: Youth Recruit Academy – Edmonton Police Service
duration: 5 full days, at spring break or in late July
eligibility: Grade 10 to 12 students with good attendance and no criminal convictions who can attend all five days from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.; a parent or guardian must attend an evening meeting
description: A five-day look at police work for 40 high school students per session. You do fitness training, team building and leadership work, plus lectures and scenarios with units like Canine, Robbery, Air 1, Traffic and Forensics. In 2026 there was a spring session (March 30 to April 2) and a summer session (July 27 to 31), with applications closing February 27. Expect a similar schedule next year.
metaDescription: Spend five days with Edmonton police units like Canine and Forensics; 40 Grade 10 to 12 students per session.

name: Student Police Academy – Calgary Police Service
provider: Calgary Police Service and the Calgary Police Youth Foundation
eligibility: Grade 12 students from Calgary and the surrounding area; spots are limited
description: A one-day academy where Grade 12 students put on a mock police uniform and duty belt, get paired with an officer mentor, and work through more than 20 realistic scenarios such as wellness checks, vehicle stops and noise complaints. It also covers crime scene analysis, collision reconstruction and surveillance. Breakfast and lunch are provided. In 2026 it ran May 13 and applications closed April 24; you apply by emailing the form.
metaDescription: A one-day Calgary police academy for Grade 12 students: an officer mentor and 20+ realistic scenarios at Heritage Park.

name: Calgary Police Cadet Corps
provider: Calgary Police Service and the Calgary Police Youth Foundation
duration: Thursday evenings September to May, plus weekend exercises; up to five years
eligibility: New members must be 12 to 16 as of the September intake; submit an application and security clearance forms
description: A free cadet program run by the Calgary Police Service. Cadets meet Thursday evenings from 5:45 to 9:15, September to May, and join weekend exercises and volunteer work. Over five levels they build leadership, fitness, first aid and marksmanship skills. Uniforms and equipment are provided. Applications for the next September intake open November 1 and close March 31, so a Grade 10 student who is still 16 can join.
metaDescription: Join Calgary's free police cadet corps at 12 to 16 for weekly leadership, fitness and first-aid training; apply November to March.

name: Calgary Stampede Showband
duration: Year-round: Tuesday evening rehearsals, a band camp weekend each month, and the Stampede in July
eligibility: Musicians, percussionists, colour guard and dancers aged 16 to 21 from Calgary and area; past music or dance experience helps, but marching experience is not needed
description: A music education and performance program in which youth aged 16 to 21 rehearse all year and perform through the 10 days of the Stampede. Rehearsals are Tuesday evenings plus one full band-camp weekend a month, with a week of full-day rehearsals right before Stampede. Auditions for the 2026-27 season were June 5 to 7, 2026 on Stampede Park. Members pay an annual fee for uniforms, equipment, instruction and local travel; tours cost extra, and there is fundraising help.
metaDescription: March, play or dance with the Calgary Stampede Showband at 16 to 21: year-round rehearsals and 10 days at Stampede.
costNote: Annual fee for uniforms, equipment, instruction and local travel (amount not posted); tours extra

name: Young Canadians School of Performing Arts – Calgary Stampede
duration: School year; Seniors train 12 to 15 hours a week, then perform in July
eligibility: Singers and dancers aged 8 to 21 from Calgary and area; Intermediates and Seniors need two years of dance, and singers need vocal training or natural ability
description: The Calgary Stampede's performing arts school, whose members sing and dance in the Grandstand Show every July. Seniors (15 to 21) train 12 to 15 hours a week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and some Sundays, and attendance is mandatory. Tuition is $2,100 a year plus a one-time fee for new members, with financial help and payment plans. Audition dates for 2027-28 are not posted yet.
metaDescription: Sing and dance in the Calgary Stampede Grandstand Show as a Young Canadian; Seniors are 15 to 21 and audition yearly.
costNote: $2,100 a year plus a one-time fee for new members; financial help and payment plans

name: Young Companies – Citadel Theatre
duration: A season of training ending in a spring production
eligibility: Actors (Young Performing Company) or technicians, designers and stage managers (Young Production Company) aged 16 to 21 who are serious about studying theatre after high school
description: Pre-professional theatre training at the Citadel in Edmonton for 16 to 21 year olds planning on theatre school or a theatre career. One cohort trains as actors and the other in production (tech, design and stage management). Local theatre professionals teach, and the season ends with a spring production in the Rice Theatre. Submissions for 2026-27 are closed; 2027-28 audition details come later.
metaDescription: Train as an actor or theatre technician with Edmonton's Citadel Theatre at 16 to 21, ending in a spring production.

name: Young Canada Works in Heritage Organizations
duration: 6 to 16 weeks, full or part time
stipend: Paid job (the wage is set by the employer)
location: Museums, archives, libraries and heritage sites across Canada
eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents or refugees aged 16 to 30 with a SIN, enrolled in high school, college or university
description: A federal program that funds summer jobs for students at museums, archives, libraries and heritage sites. High school students aged 16 or older qualify. You create an account on the Young Canada Works portal, search the posted jobs and say which interest you. There is no deadline, but most hiring is for summer, so apply in the spring. First-time participants get priority, and travel and lodging may be covered for a job more than 125 km from home.
metaDescription: Find a paid summer job at a museum, archive or heritage site through a federal program open to students 16 and older.

name: Moon Camp Challenge – European Space Agency
provider: European Space Agency (ESA) and the Airbus Foundation
eligibility: Students aged 5 to 16 in ESA member states, associate members and Canada, alone or in teams; a registered teacher or educator submits the project
description: An ESA challenge to design a habitat on the Moon, open to Canada because Canada cooperates with ESA. Use any design tool you like, from 3D modelling to games, robotics or experiments. A teacher or educator registers the team and submits on the Moon Camp site. Every valid entry gets an ESA certificate and a place in the online gallery, and teams are invited to a livestream with an astronaut. Early certificates go to entries in by April 19, 2027. Only students up to 16 qualify.
metaDescription: Design a Moon habitat for the European Space Agency's challenge, open to Canadian students up to age 16.

name: Canadian Music Competition (CMC) – Calgary Chapter
provider: Canadian Music Competition, Calgary Chapter (Canadian Music Competitions Southern Alberta Committee)
grades: Ages 7-25 (15-18 category for most high schoolers)
duration: Chapter audition in spring; national final in Montreal in July
location: Calgary audition (Edmonton candidates audition in Calgary); national final in Montreal
eligibility: Canadian citizens and permanent residents; solo performers and ensembles in age groups 7-10, 11-14, 15-18 and 19-25 (to 29 for voice)
description: A national classical music competition with a first round run by local chapters. Albertans audition with the Calgary Chapter, which also takes Edmonton candidates. Top performers go to the national final in Montreal (July 2 to 10 in 2026), where category winners are invited to play with a Canadian orchestra and scholarships are awarded. Each chapter sets its own registration deadline and fee, so contact the Calgary Chapter directly.
metaDescription: Audition in Calgary for the Canadian Music Competition; top classical players go on to the national final in Montreal.
costNote: Chapter registration fee (set by the Calgary Chapter); $200 more to compete in the national final

name: Inspirit AI Scholars
duration: 10 live sessions (25 hours) over a term, or a daily winter-break intensive
eligibility: High school students anywhere; no coding experience needed, with advanced cohorts for students who have some
description: A paid online course in artificial intelligence in groups of about five students per instructor, taught by graduates of Stanford, MIT and similar universities. You learn Python and AI basics, then build a mentored AI project for social impact. Sessions run in fall, winter and summer, and applications are rolling. The winter 2026-27 intensives run daily over the holiday break. It is expensive and not affiliated with any university, so weigh it against free options.
metaDescription: A paid online AI course for Grades 9 to 12 where you build a mentored project in small groups; no coding needed to start.
costNote: US$1,400; payment plans available

name: Alberta Youth Choir
duration: Two singing weekends and a residency in 2027
eligibility: Singers aged 16 to 22 from anywhere in Alberta; a teacher or conductor recommends you, then you audition
description: Alberta's provincial honour choir for singers aged 16 to 22, led by conductors from across Canada and abroad. For AYC 2027 your teacher or conductor recommends you by November 2, 2026, and auditions run November 23 to 28. The choir meets for a rehearsal weekend and a residency.
metaDescription: Sing in Alberta's provincial honour choir at 16 to 22; your teacher recommends you, then you audition in November.

name: Key Club – Kiwanis
location: Clubs in Brooks, Calgary, Edmonton, Lloydminster and Medicine Hat; start one with a local Kiwanis club
eligibility: High school students at a school with a Key Club, or who start one with a sponsoring Kiwanis club
description: Kiwanis's high school service club, on more than 5,000 campuses in 30 countries. Members run service projects and build leadership skills with support from a local Kiwanis club. Alberta clubs are at Brooks Composite, North Trail in Calgary, Jasper Place, J. Percy Page and Strathcona Composite in Edmonton, Holy Rosary in Lloydminster and Crescent Heights in Medicine Hat. Kiwanis Western Canada can help start one at your school.
metaDescription: Join or start a Key Club, the Kiwanis high school service club, with chapters in Calgary, Edmonton and Medicine Hat.

name: JAMHacks – High School Hackathon
eligibility: High school students from across Canada; beginners welcome
description: Canada's largest high school hackathon, held at the University of Waterloo with 200+ students building tech projects over a weekend. It is free, with meals and swag provided by sponsors, and beginners are welcome. The site does not mention travel funding, so an Alberta student would pay their own way to Ontario. JAMHacks 10 is over and JAMHacks 11 dates are not posted yet.
metaDescription: Build a tech project over a weekend at Canada's largest high school hackathon, free at the University of Waterloo.

name: Alberta Honour Wind Ensemble
duration: One ensemble weekend and concert in late winter
eligibility: High school and undergraduate wind, brass and percussion players in Alberta; individual audition by recording plus an instrumentalist questionnaire
description: Alberta's provincial honour band for high school and university players. The ensemble meets for one weekend with a guest conductor of national or international standing and ends with a concert. Admission is by individual audition: submit the questionnaire and a recording. Auditions have opened September 3 and closed December 1. There is a participation fee of $275.
metaDescription: Audition by recording for Alberta's honour band and spend a weekend with a leading guest conductor, ending in a concert.
costNote: $275 participation fee

name: Calgary Performing Arts Festival (CPAF)
eligibility: Performers from across Alberta up to age 26: solo, ensemble, chamber and speech arts
description: One of North America's largest competitive performing arts festivals, with over 3,000 entries a year. You perform for an adjudicator in music or speech arts, solo or in a group, and compete for more than $40,000 in scholarships. Registration for 2027 opens November 1, 2026 and closes January 31, 2027. Fees depend on your age, how long you perform and how many are on stage.
metaDescription: Perform for an adjudicator in Calgary's festival and compete for $40,000+ in music and speech scholarships.
costNote: Entry fee depends on age, performance length and number of performers; full refund if withdrawn by January 31

name: Edmonton Music & Speech Arts Festival (EMSAF)
duration: Two weeks in late April (April 20 to May 1 in 2026)
eligibility: Performers of any age in the Edmonton region: piano, strings, voice, winds, speech arts, musical theatre, world music, chamber groups, bands, orchestras and choirs
description: Edmonton's competitive music and speech arts festival, formerly the Edmonton Kiwanis Music Festival, with over 2,500 performances a year. You perform for an adjudicator, solo or in a group, and can enter special scholarship classes. It runs under Alberta Music Festival Association standards. Registration for 2026 closed February 5, so expect a similar deadline for 2027.
metaDescription: Perform solo or in a group for an adjudicator at Edmonton's spring music and speech arts festival, with scholarship classes.
costNote: Class entry fees on the festival's fee schedule, plus a $3.37 administration fee per entrant

name: Medicine Hat Rotary Music Festival
eligibility: Musicians in Medicine Hat and area, solo or in groups; see the syllabus for classes and rules
description: Medicine Hat's competitive music festival, where students perform for an adjudicator, from soloists to choirs, orchestras and musical theatre. It is a member of the Alberta Music Festival Association, so strong performers can be recommended on to the provincial festival. The 2027 festival runs March 8 to 21. For the 2025 festival, registration ran November 11 to January 16, so expect a similar window.
metaDescription: Perform for an adjudicator at Medicine Hat's spring music festival, with a path to the Alberta provincial festival.
costNote: Entry fee per class, set in the festival syllabus

name: Lethbridge and District Music and Speech Arts Festival
provider: Lethbridge and District Music and Speech Arts Festival
eligibility: Music and speech arts performers in Lethbridge and district, solo or in groups; see the 2027 syllabus for classes
description: Lethbridge's competitive festival for music and speech arts. You perform for an adjudicator, solo or in a group, and can win awards. The 2027 festival runs April 12 to 23, and registration is open December 1 to January 29. The 2027 syllabus lists the classes and fees.
metaDescription: Perform music or speech arts for an adjudicator at Lethbridge's April festival and compete for awards.
costNote: Entry fee per class, listed in the festival syllabus

name: Red Deer Festival of the Performing Arts
provider: Red Deer Festival of the Performing Arts Society
duration: April 13 to 15 and April 26 to May 1, 2027
location: Red Deer Polytechnic and Sunnybrook United Church, Red Deer
eligibility: Performers in Central Alberta, solo or in groups; see the festival's registration and entry fee pages
description: Central Alberta's competitive performing arts festival, with more than 1,000 student performers. You perform for an adjudicator and can be recommended on to the Alberta provincial festival; in 2026 two Red Deer entries took first place in their provincial classes. The 2027 festival runs April 13 to 15 at Red Deer Polytechnic and April 26 to May 1 at Sunnybrook United Church. Registration details for 2027 are not posted yet.
metaDescription: Perform for an adjudicator at Central Alberta's spring festival in Red Deer, with a path to the provincial festival.
costNote: Entry fee per class, listed on the festival's entry fees page

name: Grande Prairie and District Music Festival
provider: Grande Prairie and District Music Festival Association
duration: March 21 to April 30, 2027, with a Grand Concert on May 2
eligibility: Performers in Grande Prairie and district; the festival site lists age and residency rules and the Alberta and local syllabus classes
description: The Peace Country's competitive music festival. You perform for an adjudicator in classes from the Alberta and local syllabi, and top performers are featured in the Grand Concert. The 2027 festival runs March 21 to April 30, and entries close February 11, 2027. You register online through the festival site.
metaDescription: Perform for an adjudicator at Grande Prairie's spring music festival; top performers play the Grand Concert.
costNote: Entry fee per class, set in the festival syllabus

name: Alberta Provincial Music Festival
grades: By recommendation from a local festival
eligibility: Music and speech arts performers recommended by an AMFA member festival, such as Calgary, Edmonton, Lethbridge, Red Deer, Grande Prairie or Medicine Hat
description: The provincial finals for Alberta's local music festivals. You cannot enter directly: first win a recommendation at your local member festival, then compete for provincial standings and scholarships. Alberta's top provincial competitors can go on to the Canada West Performing Arts Festival, which is in Victoria, BC on July 22 to 24, 2027.
metaDescription: Earn a recommendation at your local music festival, then compete for Alberta provincial standings and scholarships.

name: Blue Ocean Student Entrepreneur Competition
duration: Pitches due February 21, 2027; winners announced in May
eligibility: High school students from any country, alone or in a team of up to five; pitches in English
description: A free online pitch competition for high school students from 170+ countries. Alone or with up to four friends, you build a business idea with the provided Blue Ocean tools and templates, then submit a pitch video of under five minutes. There are cash prizes for students and prizes for their schools. Pitches are due February 21, 2027.
metaDescription: Pitch your own business idea in a five-minute video to a free global competition for high school students.

name: Calgary Young People's Theatre (CYPT)
duration: Fall and winter class sessions, a season of productions, and summer camps
eligibility: Youth up to 18; teen classes and camps, and auditions for the season's productions (ages 9 to 18)
description: A Calgary youth theatre that runs weekly drama classes, summer camps and a season of four productions that young actors audition for. Teens have their own classes and specialty camps, including musical theatre, improv, stage makeup, and acting with stage combat. Register through the CYPT registration store.
metaDescription: Take teen drama classes and camps in Calgary, or audition for one of Calgary Young People's Theatre's four productions.
costNote: Class and camp fees vary by program

name: Alberta High School Drama Festival
provider: Alberta High School Drama Festival Association (AHSDFA)
duration: Zone festivals in April; provincial festival in May
location: Zone festivals across Alberta; provincial host changes (University of Lethbridge in 2026)
eligibility: Drama students at Alberta public, Catholic, private and charter high schools, through their school's one-act play
description: Alberta's high school one-act play festival. Your school's drama program performs a one-act play at its zone festival in April, and the plays chosen there go to the provincial festival. The provincial festival is a celebration rather than a competition, though schools are recognized and awarded. The 2026 provincial festival was May 7 to 9 at the University of Lethbridge. Ask your drama teacher to enter.
metaDescription: Perform your school's one-act play at an April zone festival and aim for Alberta's provincial drama festival in May.

name: Alberta Ballet School Summer Intensive
duration: Three weeks: June 28 to July 16 or July 19 to August 6, 2027
location: Calgary (residence available at Mount Royal University)
eligibility: Intermediate to advanced ballet students who train regularly and have several years of experience; admission by audition on the audition tour, on Zoom or by video
description: A three-week pre-professional ballet intensive at Alberta Ballet School in Calgary. Classes include ballet, pointe, pas de deux for some levels, repertoire, variations, contemporary and character dance, plus conditioning. Students in Grades 9 to 12 audition as seniors. Out-of-town students can live in residence at Mount Royal University, with supervised social activities. There are two 2027 sessions.
metaDescription: Audition for a three-week ballet intensive at Alberta Ballet School in Calgary; Grades 9 to 12 train as seniors.
costNote: Tuition not posted on the program page; residence costs extra

name: CanSat Design Challenge
provider: Canadian Satellite Design Challenge Management Society (CSDCMS)
duration: September to spring; launch campaigns in spring 2027
location: Build at school; Advanced launches near Lethbridge, AB
eligibility: Canadian students in Grades 6 to 12, in teams of up to six; no experience needed
description: Build a satellite the size of a pop can with a small computer and sensors, and fly it. Teams of up to six get a free CanSat kit by mail and follow tutorials over the fall and winter. In spring, Beginner teams' CanSats are dropped from a drone, while Advanced teams travel to Lethbridge to launch theirs by rocket to about 1 km and transmit live data. The top Advanced team represents Canada at the European Space Agency's CanSat event in the Netherlands. Registration for the 2026-27 challenge is open now.
metaDescription: Build a pop-can satellite with up to five teammates; Advanced teams launch by rocket near Lethbridge. Free kit provided.

name: Reach for the Top
duration: School year, with an Alberta provincial tournament in April and nationals in May
location: School leagues; Alberta provincials; national championship (Moncton, NB in 2026)
eligibility: High school students on their school's team of four; the school joins through a Schoolreach subscription
description: Canada's high school quiz competition, running since 1966. Teams of four buzz in on fast trivia questions across every subject. Alberta holds a provincial tournament each spring: about 216 students played at Paul Kane High School on April 18, 2026, and the winners went to the national championship in May. Ask a teacher whether your school has a team, or to start one.
metaDescription: Join your school's four-person quiz team and play toward Alberta's provincial Reach for the Top tournament.
costNote: Schools pay a Schoolreach subscription (amount not posted)

name: Write 2 Film – YouthWrite
provider: YouthWrite Society Canada, with the Calgary Society of Independent Filmmakers
duration: A week-long overnight camp in July
eligibility: Creative youth aged 14 to 19; no film experience needed
description: An overnight filmmaking camp where you go from brainstorming and writing a screenplay to screening a finished film in a week. Professional instructors teach cinematography, directing, editing, sound and acting. The 2026 camp ran July 12 to 17 and is full; 2027 dates are not posted on the camp page yet. YouthWrite offers scholarships, so ask about financial help.
metaDescription: Write, shoot and edit a short film in one week at an overnight camp near Calgary for creative teens aged 14 to 19.
costNote: $825 in 2026, including a $100 non-refundable fee; scholarships available

name: Healthcare Career Exploration Camp – Alberta Health Services
eligibility: Students going into Grades 9 to 12 who are interested in healthcare careers; participants complete training modules and a confidentiality agreement, and vaccinations are strongly recommended
description: A summer camp where you shadow healthcare workers in areas like nursing, laboratory and pharmacy, meet people across the professions, and work through patient simulation scenarios. Before starting you complete training modules, watch privacy and security videos and sign a confidentiality agreement. It costs $40 a day, with scholarships available. Applications for 2026 have closed; details for 2027 are posted June 1, 2027.
metaDescription: Shadow nurses, lab staff and pharmacists at an Alberta Health Services summer camp for students going into Grades 9 to 12.
costNote: $40 per day; scholarships available

name: Women in Engineering Day – University of Calgary
provider: Schulich School of Engineering, University of Calgary
eligibility: High school students interested in engineering, especially young women; teachers register their school
description: A day at UCalgary's engineering school aimed at high school girls: explore engineering majors and minors, meet student mentors and alumni, and hear about programs like the Bioengineering Summer Institute. Teachers register their school. The 2026 event was February 19; the 2027 date is not posted yet.
metaDescription: Spend a day at UCalgary's engineering school exploring majors and meeting mentors; aimed at high school girls.

name: Rotary Youth Program of Enrichment (RYPEN)
provider: Rotary District 5360 (southern Alberta) and District 5370 (northern Alberta)
duration: 4-day residential camp (May 7 to 10, 2027 in southern Alberta)
location: The Site, just outside Calgary (southern Alberta camp)
eligibility: Teens aged 13 to 17 during the southern Alberta camp, sponsored by a local Rotary club; grades are not a factor. Northern Alberta runs its own camp for ages 14 to 18 who live in District 5370
description: A free four-day leadership camp run by Rotary. You spend a long weekend on team activities, outdoor challenges and workshops on confidence, communication and goal setting, led by trained counsellors and peer leaders, many of them past campers. Grades do not matter. A local Rotary club sponsors you and covers the $625 cost, including meals and lodging, and arranges your ride. The southern Alberta camp is May 7 to 10, 2027; clubs confirm spots by March 31 and it fills quickly.
metaDescription: Spend a free four-day leadership weekend at Rotary's RYPEN camp near Calgary, sponsored by a local Rotary club.
